If (condition): Our jungler and nearby laners have Strong Lvl 1 and theirs don't
Then (plan): Invade their jungle on that side (steal camps / buff)
Why: Strong-dueling jungler + laner support can take 3 quadrants vs a weak duelist
Inputs used: Champion Tags: Lvl 1 for jungler + top/mid/bot
Test in Oracle's Elixir: First blood, jungle CS diff at 10

If (condition): Both teams have heavy level-1 vision and no clear Lvl 1 edge
Then (plan): Full clear ('handshake'); plan camp timing around first objective spawn instead
Why: With vision everywhere, forcing an invade gives nothing away for free
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Jungle CS diff at 10 close to 0

If (condition): Our jungler is a weak duelist vs a strong-dueling enemy jungler
Then (plan): Start on the opposite side, yield contested camps, path toward lanes with priority
Why: Contesting a stronger duelist early loses camps and time
Inputs used: Champion Tags: Jungle early / Lvl 1 for both junglers
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Jungle gold diff at 15 in these matchups

If (condition): Always
Then (plan): Start the jungle on the side away from where you want to play; finish toward the lanes with Strong laning (priority)
Why: Arrive where your laners can move first and win the 2v2 / scuttle
Inputs used: Champion Tags: Laning per lane + jungler side
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Gold diff at 10 for the lanes the jungler paths toward

If (condition): We have no lane priority on a side
Then (plan): Don't invade or fight there; play the other side
Why: Without priority the enemy collapses first
Test in Oracle's Elixir: First blood / kills at 10 when invading without priority (needs events)

If (condition): Enemy jungler is shown on one side (gank, objective, or seen)
Then (plan): Trade: invade, gank or take an objective on the opposite side; don't run across late
Why: Cross-map plays carry no counter-gank risk and beat a late counter-gank
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Not testable from OE; VOD/position data

If (condition): Early comp (Timing = Early, high early score) with bot/mid priority
Then (plan): Contest first Grubs and first Dragon; stack drakes
Why: Early comps must convert priority into objectives before they fall off
Inputs used: Champion Tags: Timing, Early score, Laning (bot/mid)
Test in Oracle's Elixir: First Grubs / first dragon win rate for early comps vs late comps

If (condition): Late / scaling comp facing an early comp
Then (plan): Don't contest early objectives; trade on the opposite side (camps, plates, other objective) and protect the scaling carry
Why: Scaling comps lose early 50/50 fights; matching or trading keeps the gap small
Inputs used: Champion Tags: Timing for both comps
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Gold diff at 15 for late comps that gave first objective vs contested it

If (condition): We are stronger at the objective (numbers or spike)
Then (plan): Start the objective; if they contest, turn and fight ('power dragon')
Why: Win-win: free objective or a favourable fight
Test in Oracle's Elixir: First dragon fights won by the comp with the earlier spike

If (condition): Objective spawning soon
Then (plan): Keep farming and arrive just in time; don't stand at the pit early
Why: Waiting wastes tempo the enemy can use elsewhere
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Not testable from OE (needs timelines)

If (condition): Our jungler is a facilitator (tank/engage) vs a carry jungler
Then (plan): Plan early ganks and plays rather than a farming race
Why: A facilitator loses the farm race; plays offset the expected gold-at-15 deficit
Inputs used: Champion Tags: Primary style, Engage for both junglers
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Jungle gold diff at 15 for facilitator-vs-carry matchups

If (condition): One of our lanes is winning
Then (plan): Don't gank it; ward its river so it can push freely. Gank lanes where the enemy jungler is confirmed far away
Why: A winning lane only needs vision; ganks are better spent elsewhere
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Not testable from OE (needs events)

If (condition): Our draft has no Strong laning in any lane and at least one Weak lane
Then (plan): Flag in draft: early game will be passive; plan safe vision and trade objectives
Why: With no priority anywhere, the enemy snowballs and you can't answer
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Gold diff at 15 and win rate for drafts with 0 Strong lanes and 1+ Weak lane

If (condition): Lane priority bot/mid after levels 2-3
Then (plan): Support and jungler ward the enemy jungle on that side; mid roams to the jungler's side
Why: Priority turns into vision and camp denial
Inputs used: Champion Tags: Laning (bot, mid), Roam / gank
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Wards placed / vision score at 15 (if available)

If (condition): Choosing between first Dragon and first Grubs
Then (plan): Default to first Dragon unless the comp or lane priority clearly favours top side
Why: Pro players cite roughly a 5% higher win rate for first Dragon than first Grubs (their claim, unverified)
Inputs used: Lane priority bot vs top; comp timing
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Win rate after first dragon vs after first Grubs, controlled for team strength. Testable directly in OE

If (condition): One of our lanes is Weak and likely to be ganked early
Then (plan): Jungler starts on that side to cover it, then paths out
Why: A losing lane that gets ganked early can be unplayable for the rest of laning. Exception to R08
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Gold diff at 10 for the weak lane when the jungler started on its side (needs start-side data)

If (condition): Planning a gank or dive
Then (plan): Hide the intent: don't walk toward the tower or clear wards in view right before committing
Why: Showing intent gives the enemy jungler time to arrive
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Not testable from OE

If (condition): Enemy starts Dragon while we have a Teleport advantage top
Then (plan): Give the Dragon; dive top or take plates instead
Why: Trading the objective for a dive and plates can be worth more than contesting
Inputs used: Summoner spell state (live), Champion Tags: Engage
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Not testable from OE (needs timelines)

If (condition): Lane opponent is missing a key early item (boots) or we hit level 6 first
Then (plan): Trade hard or threaten the all-in to force them off the wave
Why: Item and level-6 windows are the cleanest moments to win lane
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Not testable from OE (needs timelines)

If (condition): We'd be drafting a losing top matchup by default
Then (plan): Prefer an even or winning matchup unless the comp needs that pick
Why: Losing lanes repeatedly drag the early game down
Inputs used: Champion Tags: Laning for both top laners
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Top gold diff at 15 by matchup strength

If (condition): Early-strong comp with mid and bot priority
Then (plan): Push mid and bot together to convert pressure into plates; base on time rather than greed plates
Why: Pressure only counts if it turns into gold; greed gives it back
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Tower plates and gold diff at 15 for early comps

If (condition): Lane priority on both bot and top sides (or the enemy jungler is shown elsewhere)
Then (plan): Take both first scuttles
Why: Double scuttle is a clear early jungle win (gold, XP, vision)
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Not in OE directly; proxy: jungle CS/XP diff at 10

If (condition): We're ahead after the early game
Then (plan): Protect the lead: don't chase without vision or key summoners; regroup on objectives
Why: Leads are often thrown in a few bad fights right after laning
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Win rate given gold lead at 15 by league (comeback rate)

If (condition): The enemy jungler has a predictable start (same first camps, smites a buff at a set time)
Then (plan): Plan a timed invade or buff steal around his habit
Why: Level-1/2 habits are scoutable from recent games and punishable
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Not in OE; needs VOD/timelines

If (condition): A champion has hard-losing lane matchups and the enemy still holds counterpick
Then (plan): Don't blind it; blind a flex or matchup-safe pick and save the greedy pick for counterpick
Why: Blinding matchup-dependent picks hands the enemy free counters
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Lane gold diff at 15 for blind vs counter picks (OE has pick order)

If (condition): Enemy mid-jungle duo is stronger in early 2v2s than ours
Then (plan): Avoid a weak-2v2 jungler; don't contest river fights with mid before your spikes
Why: The early map is decided by the mid-jungle 2v2
Inputs used: Champion Tags: Lvl 1, Laning, Early spike for both mid-jungle duos
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Jungle + mid gold diff at 15 by duo strength

If (condition): Building the bot lane
Then (plan): Pair a roaming or weak-laning support with a self-sufficient ADC; pair a lane-dependent ADC with a lane-winning support; into dive/engage, pick an anti-dive bot lane
Why: A support that can't win lane leaves a lane-dependent ADC with nothing
Inputs used: Champion Tags: Laning, Roam / gank, Engage, Peel
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Bot gold diff at 15 by support-ADC pairing

If (condition): We picked a lane-dominant bot duo (poke / level-2 spike)
Then (plan): Play to win levels 1-3 and 6 hard; if not ahead by first base, switch to a safe plan
Why: Lane-dominant duos are feast or famine and fall off if they don't snowball
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Bot gold diff at 10 vs game result for lane-dominant duos

If (condition): Enemy bot has an enchanter (Lulu, Janna type)
Then (plan): Force the all-in before their support reaches level 6
Why: Enchanter ultimates make all-ins much harder after 6
Inputs used: Champion Tags: Primary style = Protect the carry (support)
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Not in OE (needs timelines)

If (condition): One lane is clearly winning and another can hold on its own
Then (plan): Play through the winning lane and let the safe lane soak pressure, instead of rescuing it
Why: Accelerating your carry wins more than evening out a lane that's fine anyway
Inputs used: Live lane state; Champion Tags: Wave clear
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Not in OE (needs events)

If (condition): A lane is about to reset on a natural timer
Then (plan): Jungler syncs his base with that lane so they return together
Why: Synced resets create 2-man pressure; out-of-sync bases waste tempo
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Not in OE (needs timelines)

If (condition): First scuttle / first objective about to be contested
Then (plan): Arrive with the upgraded Smite and plan camps so it's ready on time
Why: The smite edge decides early 50/50s
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Not in OE (needs timelines)

If (condition): Mid considering leaving lane to dive bot
Then (plan): Only go if the dive is near-certain and the enemy mid can't punish the free lane
Why: A free mid lead can cost more than the bot dive gains
Inputs used: Champion Tags: Roam / gank, Laning (both mids)
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Mid gold diff at 15 in games with early bot dives (needs events)

If (condition): Trading early drakes for cross-map plays
Then (plan): Track the enemy's dragon count; stop trading and contest before they reach soul point
Why: Trading works until the enemy stacks soul and the game flips
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Win rate for teams that gave the first 2-3 drakes but led gold at 15 (OE)

If (condition): Preparing for a specific opponent
Then (plan): Profile each player: gold/XP diff at 15, champion-pool size, win rate on most-played champs, strong-side vs weak-side role. Ban or pressure the predictable or weak-side player
Why: Predictable players and weak-side roles are the easiest early targets
Test in Oracle's Elixir: All computable in OE

If (condition): The enemy has a star laner
Then (plan): Draft an aggressive counter-lane into him and commit jungle pressure there early
Why: A countered star laner without jungle help can't carry; the counter needs the jungler to stick
Test in Oracle's Elixir: Star laner gold diff at 15 when countered vs not
